idea.name: Magisphere for institutions
idea.one_liner: A campus map students actually open because walking it is a game, which an institution uses to teach its biodiversity, show hazard and emergency points, and run nature trails, with adoption numbers it can report.
idea.north_star: Returning weekly walkers per campus, counted from shared finds (weeklyActivity)
non_goal: Not an official emergency or evacuation system; every DRR layer stays labelled not official until the university DRRM office signs it
Not a Roblox or Pokemon GO look-alike sold to consumers; no ads, no in-app purchases, no selling student data
Not an in-house species identification model
Not an official AIS ranking or dataset

feature_existing: Play map: 3D walk with stick or GPS, daily hunt, spawns, points, weekly streak, buddy growth stages, blind boxes
Journal and Dex on the device; camera log; Seek link; identify through an iNaturalist proxy (demo reply without a token)
Live hall: other walkers on the map with buffered interpolation, walking partners, group streak
Accounts with password and Google sign-in
Moderation: problem reports, name filter, hide/report a walker, /mod console with per-moderator tokens and an append-only audit log
Privacy: walker_id instead of player_id everywhere shared, hide-from-live-map, threatened species shared without coordinates
Campus modules: biodiversity hotspots, emergency and DRR (OSM + UP NOAH, labelled not official), a campus tree walk
Graphics tier (auto/full/lite), frame and hall benchmarks, weekly walkers on /mod
feature_in_flight: Zoomed-out play view frame rate at 4x CPU (lane reveal/perf2)
Deploy of reveal-1015 to the live URL (planned 2026-10-10, needs the owner)
Hiker 3D avatar behind ?avatar=hiker, awaiting the designer's approval
delta: An institutional deployment model: who buys, what they provide, who maintains
A compliance pack for minors and location: CPIA, consent line, breach runbook, visibility default
A lawful identify path: Pl@ntNet as primary for plants, Seek hand-off as fallback, iNaturalist CV only with written permission
Photo licence and attribution handling for iNaturalist images
A funding order and a second-campus pricing experiment

recheck.note: Gelo's 09-30 note keeps the 3D walk (judges liked it) and redirects it to institutional utility; the thesis card above is that redirection, not a new idea.
The showcase treated students as the customer. They are the users; the payer and operator is a campus office (sustainability, safety), so the persona moves to that office.
No PH product combines a campus walk game, biodiversity and DRR; incumbents are static Ateneo maps, free government hazard tools and paid US campus-map vendors (M3, M4, M10).
The plan had no money section. Running cost fits Cloudflare's free tier at one campus (B3); paid tier is USD 5/month (B1). Funding is grant-shaped, not revenue-shaped, for now.

primary_persona.who: The coordinator of a campus sustainability or biodiversity program (for Ateneo: the Institute of Sustainability / Ateneo Wild), who must engage students with the campus's living collection and report participation
primary_persona.jtbd: Run a term-long campus biodiversity walk that students do on their own time, and show the office's leadership how many walked and came back
primary_persona.today: Guided nature walks, a tree inventory and printed field guides (M8, unverified); static campus map images (M6)

secondary_segment: Campus safety / DRRM office wanting students to know hazard and help points (after the official map is provided)
Other universities in the CCC-NYC Youth Climate Leadership Accelerator HEI cohort (B5)
Parks and nature trails (eco-parks, watersheds) wanting a self-guided trail
LGU DRRMOs already trained on GeoRiskPH (M11)
accessibility: Low-end Android phones and cheap Windows laptops (graphics tier, lite mode)
Flaky campus wifi and mobile data (PWA shell, polling fallback, offline report queue)
Taglish copy; English UI with Filipino species names where curated
Minors among first-year students and visiting senior-high students (child privacy rules apply, R7)
Screen-reader users: all controls named (measured 0 of 55 unnamed), the map itself is visual

competitor.name: Ateneo static campus maps and event map pages
competitor.gap_vs_us: Images only: no position, no species, no hazard or help points, nothing a student would open twice.

competitor.name: ADMUNAV (Ateneo pedestrian wayfinding app)
competitor.gap_vs_us: Wayfinding only, Android-native; no biodiversity, hazard or reason to return; its path graph is one Magisphere asked to share.

competitor.name: Ateneo Wild guided walks and printed field guides
competitor.gap_vs_us: Needs a guide on a schedule; reaches the students who already sign up. Magisphere is the self-guided, any-time version and can carry their content.

competitor.name: HazardHunterPH / GeoRiskPH (DOST-PHIVOLCS)
competitor.gap_vs_us: Authoritative hazard reports by location, free, but not campus-scale, not walkable, and not something a student opens for fun. Magisphere should cite it, not compete.

competitor.name: UP NOAH hazard maps
competitor.gap_vs_us: Flood, landslide and surge levels by searched location; no evacuation or help points, no campus footpaths. Already a Magisphere data source (D12).

competitor.name: Seek by iNaturalist
competitor.gap_vs_us: Excellent free on-device ID and badges, but no campus, no map of where to walk, nothing an institution can configure or measure. Magisphere hands off to it.

competitor.name: Concept3D
competitor.gap_vs_us: Institutional campus maps with safety layers at about USD 85,000 a year (M3); priced for US universities, no game, no biodiversity walk.

competitor.name: Modern Campus Maps
competitor.gap_vs_us: Cheaper campus map licence (USD 6,300 a year, M4) but a directory, not an engagement tool; no PH presence found.

competitor.name: Pokemon GO / Pikmin Bloom (Scopely)
competitor.gap_vs_us: Proves students walk for a game, but the content is fiction and the institution has no say; Gelo's note is explicit that Magisphere must not read as one.

competitor.name: AllTrails
competitor.gap_vs_us: Trails with a paid tier (USD 35.99 a year) for hikers, not campus-scale, not biodiversity teaching, not institution-run.

moat: Per-campus curated ground truth that takes months to build: measured vegetation per sector, a walkable footpath graph, a species pack from the campus iNaturalist record, and the offices that have signed off each layer
A privacy and safety posture institutions can procure: no player_id shared, hide switch, threatened-species coordinates withheld, per-moderator audit log, CPIA on file
Distribution through the CCC-NYC youth climate program and its HEI cohort, where a campus hears about it from a peer campus rather than a vendor

product_form.rationale: A campus cannot self-serve this: someone must prepare its sectors, paths and species pack, collect the offices' sign-offs, and moderate. The buyer is an office that pays for a run program, so v1 is a managed deployment per campus on the shared PWA, not a product they configure alone.

rejected.why: Self-serve onboarding assumes the campus can produce its own map data and moderation; none can yet, and it hides the work that makes the moat.
A native app store build adds review delays and device targets; the PWA already runs on the low-end phones that matter and updates without a store.
No integrator is asking for campus biodiversity data as an API; the value is students walking, which an API does not produce.

v1_cut.jtbd: A campus sustainability office runs a term-long self-guided biodiversity walk and reads weekly and returning walkers on /mod
v1_cut.channel: The Ateneo Institute of Sustainability / Ateneo Wild, through the Youth CLAP team's existing Ateneo CCC relationship
v1_cut.pricing_experiment: Free pilot for Ateneo for one term in exchange for the AIS tree inventory, the official emergency map and a named moderator; the second campus is quoted a per-term fee
deferred: LGU DRRMO deployments (v1.1, needs official hazard sign-off)

page: an institution one-pager for the reveal (docs, not the app)

onboarding.why: The first screen must say what the walk is for and, for a minor, what is shared and that they can hide; the boot safety card is the place, before any live position is sent.

frontend.headline: Walk your campus. Learn what lives on it, where to go when it floods, and how to get help.

brand_brief.positioning: Campus edutech infrastructure that feels like a game to students and reads like a program to the office that runs it; never a children's game
brand_brief.audience: University students 16-22 as walkers; sustainability and safety office coordinators as the buyer
brand_brief.tone: Warm and playful on the map, plain and precise on sources, safety and data; no hype, no 'Pokemon GO clone'

backend.runtime: Cloudflare Workers with a SQLite-backed Durable Object per campus
backend.framework: Hand-rolled Worker routes (worker/sync.ts, live-socket.ts, moderation.ts) plus a Node LAN twin for booths

rejected.option: A VPS with Postgres (Neon or Gelo's own)
rejected.why: More to run and patch for a student team; the Durable Object already holds the hall, accounts and moderation and sits inside the free tier at one campus (B3).

api_boundary: /inat/identify (to be replaced by a plant identify route)
backend.data_store: Durable Object SQLite (accounts, moderation, audit) and DO storage (campus world); journals and photos stay on each phone
backend.auth: Optional accounts (password or Google); walker code to merge devices; MOD_TOKEN name:token pairs for moderators
backend.rate_limit: Per-IP brakes on reports (60/h edge), hall sockets (40/IP edge), poses (60/s/IP), wrong codes (20 per 10 min), wrong moderator tokens (10 per 15 min)
backend.observability: Frame readout (?probe=1), bench:frame and bench:hall, problem reports with diagnostics, /mod weekly activity; no third-party analytics
backend.compute: Cloudflare's edge; one Durable Object per campus ('loyola' today)

locality_rejected.why: iNaturalist's visual API is not publicly available and is fee-based by permission (D5); relying on it without written permission is the one AI path this product cannot defend.

model.name: Pl@ntNet identification API
model.task: Suggest a plant species from a photo on the camera sheet, labelled as a suggestion
model.latency_note: One HTTPS round trip per photo; 500 free identifications a day covers a campus pilot
model.privacy_note: The photo leaves the phone only when the student taps identify; no location sent

model.name: Seek by iNaturalist (on-device model v2.13)
model.task: Hand-off for animals, and for plants when the Pl@ntNet quota is spent or offline
model.privacy_note: Stores no precise location unless the user signs in (M9)

model.name: iNaturalist computer vision (score_image)
model.task: Only if iNaturalist grants written access; kept behind the existing proxy and switched off otherwise
model.latency_note: One round trip; fee and quota unknown

ai.fallback: If Pl@ntNet refuses or the daily quota runs out, the camera sheet says so and offers Open in Seek; the recorded demo reply stays for the booth only and is always labelled as recorded.
ai.retention: Identify photos are not stored by Magisphere; journals and photos stay on the phone.

data.labeling: No model training; curation is by hand: species pills (native, threatened), sector names flagged is_named_by_us, emergency features left exactly as OSM tags them.
edge_case: A photo of a whole tree at dusk on a low-end camera (poor ID input)
An animal photo sent to a plant-only service
A species absent from the campus list that Pl@ntNet suggests confidently
A threatened species whose status this repo does not carry (only curated pills are known)
An OSM emergency feature that is out of date or off campus
data.crowd_source: Students' shared finds (species, place, time; never photos or notes) under their consent line, with threatened species' coordinates withheld and hidden walkers anonymised.

risk.name: Minors' location shown to strangers (Data Privacy Act, NPC child guidance)
risk.mitigation: Complete a CPIA with the university DPO before the pilot; default live visibility to partners-only or off for the pilot; consent line on the boot card; hide switch stays
risk.kill_switch: If no CPIA is signed off by 2026-10-13, the reveal runs with the live hall off (no positions shared) and the pilot does not start

risk.name: Harassment or stalking through the live map
risk.mitigation: Hide and report on every name tag, /mod hide with audit, escalation to the university's CODI (R11)
risk.kill_switch: Any credible stalking report during the pilot turns the hall off campus-wide within 24 hours until the moderator and CODI review it

risk.name: Using iNaturalist's visual API without permission
risk.mitigation: Switch the primary to Pl@ntNet, keep Seek as the fallback, email iNaturalist for written terms
risk.kill_switch: No iNaturalist token ships in any deployed build after 2026-10-10 unless iNaturalist has answered in writing

risk.name: Photo licences: CC BY-NC or all-rights-reserved images on species cards
risk.mitigation: Store licence and photographer per photo, show attribution, and for any paid campus use only CC0/CC BY photos or the curated art
risk.kill_switch: A paid deployment does not go live while any card shows an image without a recorded compatible licence

risk.name: The unofficial emergency layer is read as official
risk.mitigation: Not-official line leads the panel and the route card; OSM-only data; the DRRM office asked to provide the official map
risk.kill_switch: If the DRRM office or CFMO objects, the emergency module is switched off for that campus the same day

risk.name: Nobody maintains it after the reveal
risk.mitigation: Named maintainer and moderator rota in the pilot agreement; costs inside the free tier
risk.kill_switch: Fewer than 20 weekly walkers on /mod for four consecutive pilot weeks pauses the program and triggers a re-plan

risk.name: A personal-data breach
risk.mitigation: Store little (no photos, no player_id shared, reports deleted after 30 days); a written 72-hour notice runbook naming who tells the NPC, the children and their parents
risk.kill_switch: Any confirmed breach stops sign-ups and the hall until the NPC notice and the parents' notice have gone out

ai_multiplier.note: Building with Claude lanes compresses code, tests and docs; it does not compress the university's sign-offs, the CPIA, data sharing or walking the trail on campus

acquirer_type: A university that adopts it as its own platform

open_question: Who sees whom in the live hall by default for a university deployment: everyone, partners only, or nobody until the student opts in?
Is Magisphere a personal information controller or a processor for the university, and who registers, appoints the DPO and notifies breaches?
Will iNaturalist grant a student campus app written access to its visual API, and at what fee?
Does Pl@ntNet's free plan allow a key used from a web app and non-affiliated use, or should the team apply for the non-profit plan?
Does the university's policy allow location features for students under 18, and does it want a parental consent path?
Which fund can a team that is not DTI/SEC-registered apply to in 2026, and are the CLAP seed figures in the repo real?
What is the second campus, and what would it actually pay per term?
Who maintains Magisphere after the Youth CLAP program ends, and for how long?
